messages:
June (AE): Ardent POC report: customer ran a stress warmup to simulate peak traffic (50 parallel clients) and now sees TTFT tails ~1.5-2s and intermittent 429s. They used batch=28 + client prefetch across all threads. Can SE/SRE help triage and provide a quick Dedicated trial ballpark?
Kofi (SE): Oof. Which model/runtime and average/peak context? Any client logs?
June (AE): Model: ardent-13b (fp16). Avg prompt ~320 tokens, peaks ~1024. Client log shows repeated "kv_shard_lock_timeout" and our gateway returning 429 clustered after the warmup. They're also asking about KMS key residency and the security questionnaire for Dedicated.
Diego (ML): kv_shard_lock_timeout + large batch + many simultaneous prefetches = classic cache lock contention + working-set blowout. With long contexts, decoding buffers add memory pressure which increases eviction and lowers prefix-hit ratio.
Rina (SRE): Infra view: tenant active requests spiked at 2110012200; per-tenant concurrency guard engaged and returned 429s. Router ingress backlog increased and KV eviction rate rose at 2110012212. This lines up with the client's warmup pattern.
Kofi (SE): Immediate guidance to share with customer: 1) stop all-clients simultaneous prefetch; 2) reduce batch size to 8-12 (max_requests); 3) lower batching window (max_delay_ms) to reduce formation latency; 4) enable streaming=true so first bytes arrive sooner; 5) use staged prefetch or jittered warmup. Example client snippet to send them:
```json
{"batch": {"max_requests": 12, "max_delay_ms": 6}, "prefetch": "staged", "stream": true}
```
June (AE): They asked if Dedicated will fix this and for a quick quote to justify the ask to security/compliance teams.
Sam (Sales Ops): Quick presales note: Dedicated isolates cache and egress from noisy neighbors and gives deterministic shard placement which reduces eviction due to other tenants. Ballpark for an entry Dedicated pod (8x GPU class) with standard support is "~$Pk/month"; private networking, KMS integration, and premium SLAs add to that. I'll issue an exact quote if you want me to.
Diego (ML): Important: Dedicated helps but does not prevent poor warmup patterns. Recommend staged prefetch (server-side) via our endpoint /v1/prefetch?mode=staged which sequences per-shard prefetch, or orchestrate client-side jittered prefetch. Also re-benchmark if they change quantization (e.g., FP4) since some decode kernels can increase tail latency at long contexts.
Rina (SRE): I can temporarily raise their per-tenant concurrency cap from 30 -> 48 for a 90-minute controlled replay and monitor queue depth + eviction rate. Will rollback if eviction rate exceeds safe thresholds. OpsBot will post when bumping.
SecBot: sec/questionnaire/ardent-poc: security questionnaire requested by customer at 2110012290. Items flagged: KMS key residency, SOC2 attestation, data retention policy. Please assign SecOps review.
Kofi (SE): Also ask the customer to collect request traces: include X-Request-ID on a slow request and provide curl -v output. We need one trace during warmup, one during steady-state, and one during a reproduced spike. That will show time split across gateway/router/runtime and confirm whether runtime was decoding or waiting on KV locks. Example trace curl:
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-Request-ID: trace-123" -v https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"model":"ardent-13b","input":"..."}'
```
Kofi (SE): Short-term message to customer to copy: "Please run a phased warmup: stagger clients with a 200-500ms jitter, set batch.max_requests=12 and max_delay_ms=6, set stream=true, and use /v1/prefetch?mode=staged for any prefetch activity. If you still see 429s, send us three traces (warmup/steady/spike) and we'll run a temporary concurrency bump to replay."
June (AE): Customer also sent the security questionnaire attachment and wants to know if KMS keys can be customer-managed in Dedicated and whether data residency is possible.
Sam (Sales Ops): For Dedicated we support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) and VPC/private deployments for regional residency. I'll coordinate with SecOps to populate the questionnaire and provide SOC2/ISO artifacts. Expect initial answers within 24-48 hours.
Diego (ML): One more tech note: for first-token sensitive experiences, consider prefix-level pre-caching for top prompts and short-circuit logic for deterministic templates. We can draft a 10-prompt pre-cache plan to reduce TTFT for common flows.
Rina (SRE): I'll stand by to apply the temporary concurrency bump when they replay. I'll monitor eviction rate, queue depth, and per-shard lock timeouts; will revert if tail metrics worsen.
June (AE): Action items: 1) I'll send the tuned client snippet and phased warmup instructions to the customer; 2) request three traces and the curl examples; 3) Sam will start Dedicated trial quote and SecOps will begin questionnaire; 4) Rina will provision temporary concurrency bump window when requested. Re-open thread if 429s/TTFT persist after controlled replay. :raised_hands:
